data.rationale: EDR detection of endpoint beaconing to suspected C2 server indicates active malware communication. Host WS-ACCT-07 shows outbound communication pattern consistent with command and control activity. Hash artifact suggests executable/malicious payload involvement. High severity due to confirmed malicious behavior and command infrastructure communication, though "suspected" C2 designation prevents critical classification.

data.summary: Host WS-ACCT-07 is running an unsigned trojan binary (svch0st.exe, hash ab12cd34ef56) spawned from a temp directory [search_alerts-0/A2, search_alerts-7, lookup_ioc-2]. This process makes periodic HTTPS network connections to 198.51.100.7:443 [get_logs-4, get_logs-5, get_logs-6], which EDR flagged as a 60-second beacon [search_alerts-0/A1, search_alerts-8]. That destination IP is confirmed-malicious Cobalt Strike C2 infrastructure [lookup_ioc-1], resolving the original "suspected C2" qualifier. The affected asset is a high-criticality Windows 11 workstation owned by Accounting [get_asset_context-3], raising financial-data exposure risk.
data.hypothesis: WS-ACCT-07 is infected with Cobalt Strike malware masquerading as svch0st.exe and is actively beaconing to confirmed C2 infrastructure at 198.51.100.7.

unsupported_claims: The summary attributes the trojan classification to lookup_ioc-2, but lookup_ioc-2 provides no indication of WHICH IOC it describes (no hash/filename echoed back). The link between lookup_ioc-2's 'trojan' reputation and svch0st.exe/ab12cd34ef56 is an inference, not directly grounded.

Similarly, lookup_ioc-1 returns only {reputation, categories} with no echoed indicator; the claim that 198.51.100.7 specifically is the 'confirmed-malicious Cobalt Strike C2' relies on assuming lookup_ioc-1 was queried for that IP. This attribution is plausible but not self-evidenced by the item's content.

The phrase 'periodic HTTPS network connections ... which EDR flagged as a 60-second beacon' overstates the log evidence: get_logs-4/5/6 show only two connections each, 60 seconds apart (11:00 and 11:01). Two data points do not establish a sustained periodic beacon; the '60-second beacon' characterization comes solely from the alert text, not from the logs.
gaps: get_logs-4, get_logs-5, and get_logs-6 are three identical copies of the same two log lines. This appears to be redundant/duplicated evidence rather than three independent corroborating sources, which artificially inflates the apparent weight of the network evidence. The finding cites them as if independent.

No evidence confirms which indicator lookup_ioc-1 and lookup_ioc-2 were queried against. The reputation lookups should echo the queried IOC to firmly bind reputation to 198.51.100.7 and ab12cd34ef56 respectively.
Log evidence spans only ~1 minute (11:00-11:01Z). No evidence of ongoing/current beaconing, so the claim the host is 'actively beaconing' is only supported for a narrow past window.
No evidence of data exfiltration or lateral movement despite the 'financial-data exposure risk' framing; the risk is inferred from asset criticality/owner only.
No evidence covering scope beyond WS-ACCT-07 (e.g., whether other hosts contacted 198.51.100.7 or ran svch0st.exe).

data.summary: WS-ACCT-07, a high-criticality Windows 11 host owned by Accounting [get_asset_context-14], ran an unsigned binary svch0st.exe (hash ab12cd34ef56) spawned from a temp directory [search_alerts-9, search_alerts-11, search_alerts-18]. That process made outbound connections to 198.51.100.7:443 at 11:00Z and 11:01Z on 2026-06-28 [get_logs-15], corroborating an EDR alert of a periodic 60s beacon to 198.51.100.7 [search_alerts-9, search_alerts-10]. Threat-intel returned two malicious verdicts: one c2/cobalt-strike [lookup_ioc-12] and one trojan [lookup_ioc-13, lookup_ioc-20]. Scope: no evidence of exfiltration [get_logs-23], lateral movement [get_logs-24], or spread of svch0st.exe to other hosts [get_logs-22]; observed C2 traffic involves only WS-ACCT-07 [get_logs-21].
data.hypothesis: WS-ACCT-07 was compromised by malware masquerading as svchost.exe (svch0st.exe, hash ab12cd34ef56) executed from a temp directory [search_alerts-9], which established a 60-second C2 beacon over TCP/443 to 198.51.100.7 [search_alerts-9, get_logs-15]. Threat intel flags both indicators as malicious, consistent with a Cobalt Strike-style implant [lookup_ioc-12, lookup_ioc-13]. Confirmed impact is limited to this single high-criticality host [get_asset_context-14] for the observed window 11:00-11:01Z only [get_logs-15]. CAVEATS: (1) Beaconing is evidenced only within a ~1-minute past window (11:00-11:01Z); there is no evidence of ongoing/current beaconing [get_logs-15]. (2) get_logs-4/5/6, get_logs-15/16/17, and get_logs-21 are byte-identical copies of the SAME two log lines, i.e. one source, not independent corroboration. (3) The lookup_ioc results do not echo the queried indicator, so the IP->c2 [lookup_ioc-12] and hash->trojan [lookup_ioc-13] bindings are inferred from query order, not proven by tool output. (4) No data exfiltration [get_logs-23] or lateral movement [get_logs-24] is evidenced; any 'financial-data exposure risk' is inferred solely from asset criticality/owner [get_asset_context-14]. (5) No evidence of scope beyond WS-ACCT-07: no other host ran svch0st.exe [get_logs-22] or appears in C2 logs [get_logs-21].

unsupported_claims: Summary claims get_logs-21 shows 'observed C2 traffic involves only WS-ACCT-07' - but get_logs-21 contains no host field; the log lines never explicitly name a host, so attributing them to WS-ACCT-07 (or asserting exclusivity) is an inference not directly proven by get_logs-21.

The binding of 198.51.100.7 -> c2/cobalt-strike [lookup_ioc-12] and hash ab12cd34ef56 -> trojan [lookup_ioc-13/20] is unsupported by tool output, since none of the lookup_ioc results echo the queried indicator. The findings' own caveat (3) acknowledges this, but the summary still states the bindings as fact.

The netconn logs (get_logs-15 etc.) do not contain a hash; linking hash ab12cd34ef56 to the outbound-connecting process is an inference joining search_alerts (hash) with get_logs (process name), not directly evidenced in a single item.
gaps: No independent corroboration of the beacon: get_logs-4/5/6/15/16/17/21 are byte-identical copies of the same two log lines (one source). The findings correctly flag this, but it means the '60s beacon' periodicity is only asserted by EDR alert text, not proven by multiple observations.
Beaconing evidence is confined to an 11:00-11:01Z window on 2026-06-28; no evidence of current/ongoing activity or of how the binary arrived (initial access vector).

get_logs-22/23/24 return 'No matching logs' - absence of results is not the same as proof of no lateral movement/exfiltration/spread; query scope and coverage are unknown, so negative conclusions are weakly supported.
Threat-intel queries lack indicator echo, so it is unverifiable which reputation verdict maps to which IOC; a re-query capturing the queried indicator is warranted.
The log lines lack a host field; a query correlating the netconn events to WS-ACCT-07 (and confirming no other host) would close the attribution gap.

data.executive_summary: On 2026-06-28 between 11:00–11:01Z, EDR telemetry detected a high-criticality Windows 11 workstation (WS-ACCT-07), owned by the Accounting department, executing an unsigned binary named svch0st.exe (SHA256: ab12cd34ef56) launched from a temporary directory. The binary masquerades as the legitimate Windows svchost.exe process and established outbound connections over TCP/443 to 198.51.100.7, with a periodic 60-second beacon pattern consistent with Cobalt Strike command-and-control (C2) infrastructure. Threat intelligence returned malicious verdicts for both the IP address (C2/Cobalt Strike) and the file hash (Trojan). At this time, the confirmed impact is isolated to WS-ACCT-07; no evidence of data exfiltration, lateral movement, or spread to other hosts was observed within the queried log scope. However, several evidentiary gaps remain — including unconfirmed indicator-to-verdict bindings, a single-source log dataset, and a narrow one-minute observation window — and further investigation is warranted before definitive scope conclusions can be drawn. Given the host's high criticality and access to financial data, immediate containment is recommended.

2026-06-28 (investigation window) — Log queries for lateral movement (get_logs-24), exfiltration (get_logs-23), and spread of svch0st.exe to other hosts (get_logs-22) returned no matching results. Scope of query coverage is unconfirmed; negative results do not constitute proof of absence.
